(a) Each horizontal surface other than a main wing, must be designed for loads resulting from –
  (1) Gust velocities specified in CS 23.333 (c) with flaps retracted; and
  (2) Positive and negative gusts of 7.62 m/s (25 fps) nominal intensity at VF corresponding to the flight conditions specified in CS 23.345 (a) (2).
(b) Reserved.
(c) When determining the total load on the horizontal surfaces for the conditions specified in sub-paragraph (a) , the initial balancing loads for steady unaccelerated flight at the pertinent design speeds, VF, VC and VD must first be determined. The incremental load resulting from the gusts must be added to the initial balancing load to obtain the total load.
(d) In the absence of a more rational analysis, the incremental load due to the gust must be computed as follows only on aeroplane configurations with aft-mounted, horizontal surfaces, unless its use elsewhere is shown to be conservative: ροKgUdeVahtSht ⎛ dε ⎞ ΔLht = ⎜1 − ⎟ ⎝ dα ⎠ 2 where – Δ Lht = Incremental horizontal tail load (N); ρo = Density of air at sea-level (kg/m3) Kg = Gust alleviation factor defined in CS 23.341; Ude = Derived gust velocity (m/s); V = Aeroplane equivalent speed (m/s); aht = Slope of aft horizontal tail lift curve (per radian); Sht = Area of aft horizontal tail (m2); and ⎛ dε ⎞ ⎜1 − ⎟ = Downwash factor ⎝ dα ⎠
